neighbours.label: Marine-megafauna context feature that peaks on the list connector (',', ' and', ' and the') right before another headline sea-animal species name is expected, sharks above all (also rays, dolphins, tuna); the same list frame filled with freshwater fish, seabirds, invertebrates or land animals stays low, and whether small reef fish also stay low is the boundary this test probes.
fire: Along the outer wall, the guides pointed out blacktip, grey reef and silvertip sharks patrolling the current.
The sanctuary protects whale sharks, scalloped hammerheads and oceanic whitetips that gather around the seamount each spring.
Fishermen in the gulf complained that bull sharks, spinner sharks and the occasional great hammerhead were stealing their catch.
Spearfishers off the point have learned to expect dusky sharks, blacknose sharks and the odd mako trailing their catch up to the boat.
Beyond the breakers, lifeguards have logged great whites, bull sharks and the odd tiger shark in recent weeks.
Boat tours out of the harbour usually find bottlenose, common and Risso's dolphins feeding along the shelf edge.
The shallow flats of the lagoon are a nursery for southern stingrays, cownose rays and the occasional manta.
Longliners working the warm current target yellowfin, bigeye and albacore tuna, along with the odd swordfish.
quiet: Fly fishers on the upper river still take brook trout, cutthroat and the occasional mountain whitefish before the water warms.
Electrofishing in the lower reaches turned up pike, perch and a handful of large bream.
The island's cliffs are crowded with gannets, razorbills and fulmars from April to August.
Rock-poolers at low tide turn up hermit crabs, limpets and beadlet anemones within minutes of starting.
Dredge samples from the offshore sites consisted mainly of urchins, whelks and sea cucumbers (Okafor and Lind 2011).
The volunteers spent the morning counting sharks from the dive boat, then sorted their gear, rinsed the cameras and logged the dive.
The house reef is busy with damselfish, wrasse and juvenile parrotfish, none of them longer than a hand.
On the headland path, walkers often see rabbits, skylarks and the occasional adder stretched out in the sun.

predictions: Shark-list fires (idx 0-4) >= 0.45 at ',' or ' and' (probe analogue 0.773 at ' and'; corpus 229/220). Dolphin, ray and tuna fires (idx 5-7) have no probe support: expect 0.15-0.50, tuna weakest and possibly below 0.20. Expect 6/8 fire >= 0.30, median >= 0.35. Near misses: freshwater (x2), seabird, land and academic items 0.01-0.12 (analogues 0.093, 0.038, 0.011, 0.062); rock-pool, counting-sharks and house-reef items ride the ~0.15 marine baseline (analogues 0.148, 0.152, 0.144) and may land 0.12-0.30; the house-reef small-fish list is the discriminating item and the one near miss allowed >= 0.30 (could reach 0.40 given the lionfish corpus hit). AUROC ~0.90-0.96; the test fails on AUROC rather than the median if the three non-shark fires all land under the three marine near misses, or if two near misses reach 0.30. If only the non-shark fires fail, the label narrows to sharks; if the house-reef item fires, the label gains 'small reef fish not excluded'.
notes: Only high probe: 'nurse, lemon and tiger sharks' 0.773 at ' and'; all else <= 0.27. Corpus: 'bull⟦ and⟧ reef sharks' 229, 'oceanic whitetip⟦,⟧ scalloped hammerhead' 220, 'with⟦ the⟧ Smooth Stingray' 170, 'common dolphin⟦,⟧ bottlenose' 131, 'by⟦ a⟧ shark' 113, tuna 93: peak = token before the species name, never the name. Bare determiner 'knocked into the water by a humpback whale' 0.052 (peak ' whale'): the species must already be predictable; determiner frame dropped. Lows: trout 0.093, aquarium 0.144, coral/clams 0.148, academic polychaetes 0.062, seabirds 0.038, lions 0.011, shark survey->hotel 0.152, fisheries 0.162, word-sense and floor controls <= 0.09. Small-reef-fish exclusion rests on one corpus peak position (' like' sharks 94.5 over the gobies/blennies connectors), not a probe, and 'threat⟦ invasive⟧ lionfish' hits 92 (0.40): the house-reef near miss is the direct test. Offshoot: habitat/sediment slots at 0.24-0.27 (beach/sand 0.239, seabed sediment 0.237, river silt 0.267; 'inner and⟦ outer⟧ reefs' 109.5; logit promotes ' sediment', ' Clay'): near misses avoid slots where reef/coral/beach/sand/sediment/lagoon is the predictable next word; fires may contain them. Opposite pole: fluvial/limnology and academic geoscience lists ('lotic⟦ and⟧ lentic', 'fluvial geomorphology⟦,⟧', karst); logit suppresses ' stream', ' channel'. Tokens: ',', ' and', ' the', ' odd', ' occasional' single; species names split after the read position; 'bronze whalers' (' wh'+'alers') dropped.
